author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Television’s biggest awards race reaches its ceremony Monday night, with The Pitt and Hacks among the programs drawing attention at the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards in Los Angeles.

The Pitt is competing for best drama for the second consecutive year. The medical series is part of a field that includes established television franchises and newer streaming hits, as voters weigh the season’s most widely recognized performances.

Hacks star Jean Smart could win comedy actress for another season, while Harrison Ford is in contention for his first Emmy at age 84. The report also identified the limited series Widow’s Bay as a late entrant attracting momentum.

The ceremony is scheduled for 8 p.m. Eastern on NBC and Peacock, with Mariska Hargitay as host. More than 27,000 Television Academy members vote on the awards, so the preview reflects the competitive field rather than final results.
The report remains subject to further verified updates as officials continue reviewing the circumstances.
dek: The 78th Primetime Emmy Awards will air Monday night with The Pitt defending its drama presence and Hacks’ Jean Smart chasing another comedy-acting win.
headline: The Pitt, Hacks headline Emmy race ahead of Monday night ceremony
